items.title: Arturo O'Farrill interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2024
items.q: I fell in love with Herbie Hancock.

ctx.x: If I don’t ask this I’m going to wonder later on, you’ve used the word “sovereignty” a few times. Can you enlighten me on what that means to you?

What that means to me is that I don’t have to adhere to structures that are foisted upon me. The whole idea of being a musician was a choice, it was a willful one. I was exposed to music through my father but I fell in love with Herbie Hancock. I chose to do music I love regardless of what the paycheck is. My father didn’t. My father struggled with creating a commercial music house for jingles. I’ve chosen to be who I am to engage in conversations about racial, ethnic identity, physical identity, sexual identity.…
Wonderful. I’ll wrap up with just two brief things. I wanted to just make a comment on how wonderful I thought it was that you were able to return to Cuba and put your father to rest there.
